content.user_title: Improve Jest Tests with Proven Patterns
content.value_statement: Jest tests often become brittle when data, mocks, and assertions are inconsistent. This skill provides practical patterns for TDD, factories, mocking, and behavior-focused tests.
actual_capabilities: Explains a red-green-refactor workflow for writing tests before production code.
Shows reusable factory functions for component props and test data.
Demonstrates Jest module mocks and generated GraphQL hook mocks.
Provides Testing Library query patterns for present, absent, and asynchronous elements.
Outlines user interaction tests using fireEvent and waitFor.
Lists simple npm commands for running all tests, coverage, or one test file.
limitations: Focuses on Jest and React Native Testing Library examples.
Does not configure test runners, Babel, TypeScript, or CI pipelines.
Does not include advanced integration, end-to-end, or performance testing patterns.
Assumes the user adapts placeholder components, imports, and data types.

use_cases.title: Write Component Unit Tests
use_cases.description: Create behavior-focused tests for rendering, loading states, edge cases, and user actions.

use_cases.title: Standardize Test Data Setup
use_cases.description: Replace repeated object literals with factory functions that provide defaults and clear overrides.

use_cases.title: Mock Generated Data Hooks
use_cases.description: Mock modules and GraphQL hooks so tests can cover success, empty, loading, and error states.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Component Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Use testing-patterns to write a Jest test for this React Native component. Focus on visible behavior and use Testing Library queries.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Props Factory
prompt_templates.prompt: Use testing-patterns to create a reusable props factory for this component. Include sensible defaults and override support.

prompt_templates.title: Mock a GraphQL Hook
prompt_templates.prompt: Use testing-patterns to mock this generated GraphQL hook. Add tests for loading, empty, error, and success states.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Brittle Test Suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Use testing-patterns to review this Jest test file. Replace implementation-detail assertions with behavior checks and extract factories where useful.

output_examples.input: A component needs tests for default rendering and a button press.
output_examples.output: A focused test plan with a custom render helper, default props factory, visible text assertion, and interaction assertion.

output_examples.input: A GraphQL-backed screen needs loading, empty, and success coverage.
output_examples.output: A mock strategy for the generated hook plus separate test cases for each user-visible state.

output_examples.input: A test file repeats user objects with inconsistent fields.
output_examples.output: A reusable user factory with default fields and examples for overriding only the fields under test.

best_practices: Write the failing test first, then add only the production code needed to pass.
Use factory functions for props and data so tests stay consistent and easy to update.
Assert public behavior through visible output and user interactions.
anti_patterns: Do not test implementation details that users cannot observe.
Do not assert only that a mock function was called when real behavior can be checked.
Do not duplicate large test data objects across many test cases.

faq.question: What testing stack does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Jest with React Native Testing Library, and it can be adapted to similar Testing Library setups.

faq.question: Can this skill create test factories?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows factories with defaults and override objects for component props and domain data.

faq.question: Does this skill support TDD?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends writing a failing test, adding minimal code, then refactoring after the test passes.

faq.question: Can it help with mocked modules?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Jest module mock examples and generated GraphQL hook mock patterns.

faq.question: Does it replace project-specific test setup?
faq.answer: No. Users still need their project imports, providers, runner configuration, and environment setup.

faq.question: Is it suitable for end-to-end testing?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on unit and component tests, not browser or device automation flows.
